# Kickoff: platform posts (rev 7, 2026-10-15)

Matched to essay.md rev 7. Each one tells the same idea from a different angle. Approve each one separately. Paste [LINK] only after the Substack post is live.

## LinkedIn

For weeks I've been building the tool that was supposed to help me post about my work. So I didn't post about my work.

The first draft of my introduction even had a blank in it: "add the first real handoff here." I couldn't publish until my agents had taken something over, and they couldn't take anything over until I finished the app. So I kept building the app.

Today I changed one word. I'm not reporting that I've *handed over* the keys to my agents. I'm *handing them over*, a little at a time, in public.

The practice is called Agents for Introverts. It starts with the work, not the feed. My agents recover what I actually did, we talk it through, and that conversation becomes a piece I can share in different forms. You're reading the LinkedIn version. The full story is on Substack.

For now I review every word and publish by hand. I'll share what the agents take on, what I correct, and what helps.

What's a decision from your own work that someone else could learn from, but you've never written up?

[LINK]

Made with Agents for Introverts. The experience and point of view are mine; my agent helped shape this version.

## Publish checklist (about 20 minutes once the essay reads right)

1. Read essay.md. Fix the [CONFIRM] line and anything that doesn't sound like you. Delete the HTML comment.
2. Substack: paste the essay into a new post at agentsforintroverts.substack.com and publish. Send it to subscribers.
3. Copy the post URL into [LINK] in all three posts.
4. Post LinkedIn, then X, then Threads. Each one only after you've reread it.
5. Paste the four live URLs into receipts.md (same folder) so the next session can pick up replies.
